1	# ngrrram
2	
3	`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
4	particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
5	layouts effectively.
6	
7	![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)
8	
9	Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
10	these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
11	example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
12	Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
13	making strong use of ngrams.
14	
15	There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
16	[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
17	inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.
18	
19	However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
20	which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
21	layout I was still learning.
22	
23	Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
24	ones.
25	
26	## Installation
27	
28	### Releases
29	
30	Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
31	linux, windows and macos are available.
32	
33	### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))
34	
35	Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:
36	
37	```bash
38	yay -S ngrrram-git
39	or
40	yay -S ngrrram-bin
41	```
42	
43	### From Source
44	
45	Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:
46	
47	```bash
48	cargo build --release
49	```
50	
51	The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`
52	
53	### Looking for help packaging!
54	
55	If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!
56	
57	## Usage
58	
59	`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
60	flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.
61	
62	Options:
63	```
64	Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]
65	
66	Options:
67	  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
68	  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
69	  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
70	  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
71	  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
72	  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
73	      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
74	      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
75	      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
76	      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
77	      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
78	  -h, --help              Print help
79	```
80	
81	If you start `ngrrram` without parameters, it uses these recommended defaults:
82	```bash
83	ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100
84	```
85	
86	## Layout Emulation
87	
88	To emulate a different keyboard layout in `ngrrram`, you must pass the flags
89	`--emu-in` and `--emu-out`, the first one describing your current layout, and
90	the second one being the one you want to emulate.
91	
92	Available layouts are:
93	
94	- `qwerty`    (Qwerty)
95	- `qwertz`    (Qwertz)
96	- `azerty`    (Azerty)
97	- `dvorak`    (Dvorak)
98	- `colemak`   (Colemak)
99	- `colemakdh` (ColemakDH)
100	
101	> Having to provide an input layout is sub-optimal. I'm not sure how to get
102	> layout independent scancodes in rust; Could not get `device_query` to work.
103	> If you know a solution, please tell me.
104	
105	## Random Notes
106	- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of
107	  that lesson; no need to stress.
108	- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.
109	  Otherwise WPM would unnaturally skyrocket with smaller ngrams.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Drive ./executable under a pty, send keys, capture raw output."""
import os, pty, sys, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, argparse

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--args', default='', help='args for executable')
    ap.add_argument('--keys', default='', help='keystrokes: literal, \\n=enter, ESC=x1b; use ;delay syntax |key:delay_ms|')
    ap.add_argument('--rows', type=int, default=24)
    ap.add_argument('--cols', type=int, default=80)
    ap.add_argument('--settle', type=float, default=0.8, help='wait after spawn before keys')
    ap.add_argument('--after', type=float, default=0.5, help='wait after last key')
    ap.add_argument('--out', default='/tmp/cap.bin')
    a = ap.parse_args()

    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.environ['TERM'] = 'xterm-256color'
        argv = ['./executable'] + (a.args.split() if a.args else [])
        os.execv('./executable', argv)
        os._exit(127)

    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', a.rows, a.cols, 0, 0))
    out = b''
    def drain(timeout):
        nonlocal out
        end = time.time() + timeout
        while time.time() < end:
            r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], max(0, end - time.time()))
            if fd in r:
                try:
                    chunk = os.read(fd, 65536)
                except OSError:
                    break
                if not chunk:
                    break
                out += chunk

    drain(a.settle)
    # keys format: chunks separated by |, each chunk is text to send, optional :ms delay after
    for chunk in a.keys.split('|'):
        if not chunk:
            continue
        text, _, d = chunk.partition(':')
        data = text.encode().decode('unicode_escape').encode('latin1')
        os.write(fd, data)
        drain(float(d or 300) / 1000.0)
    drain(a.after)
    with open(a.out, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(out)
    try:
        os.write(fd, b'\x03')  # ctrl-c to exit
    except OSError:
        pass
    drain(0.3)
    try:
        os.close(fd)
    except OSError:
        pass
    try:
        os.waitpid(pid, 0)
    except ChildProcessError:
        pass
    print(f'captured {len(out)} bytes -> {a.out}', file=sys.stderr)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
